survives: white masthead with glyph + bold name
pale ground, white bordered cards, one green accent
bound_to_product: copy: tool names, deposits, sessions, "the desk", volunteer voice
the session-day marking concept (but not its rendering)
evidence.name_hidden: With the name hidden a reader can tell it lends equipment from the copy, not from any visual element.

evidence.predicted_default: Pale or white ground, one friendly green/teal accent, white rounded cards in a grid with an icon per item, public-service form patterns (error summary, radio cards), one system-like sans.
evidence.predicted_opposite: A warm workshop look: kraft/pegboard textures, stencil or slab display type, hazard-yellow accents.
evidence.matching: Every identity-carrying element matches the default: ground, accent, card grid, repeated icon, form patterns, single sans. Nothing matches the opposite.

evidence.brief: Reservation pages for a volunteer-run toy library in a village hall, collected on Saturday mornings.
evidence.predicted: Light ground, one accent, card grid with placeholder icons, a date grid, a confirmation card.
evidence.overlap: Near-total; only the words would change. The calendar with session tags would also be produced by that brief.

evidence: Swap fails: the frame (white masthead with a small stroke glyph and the name in bold body sans, pale grey-green ground, white 4px-bordered cards, one dark-green filled button, red-bordered error summary) would carry a council library booking or a sports-club kit hire unchanged; only the copy (tool names, deposits, 'Open' sessions) binds it to Fernhill.

Category-guess fails: predicted default for a volunteer-run community booking flow is a pale ground, one green accent, white cards, a public-service style error summary and native controls; every identity-carrying element matches it.
Similar-prompt fails: 'reservation pages for a community seed library / toy library' would land on the same green-accent card grid with a repeated generic icon in each thumbnail.

The membership-card green cited in the brief is not perceivable as a membership card: it is a standard action green; nothing from the library's physical world (the card, the room, tool tags, the Saturday list) appears.

Closest thing to a signature is the pick-up calendar with 'Open' tags / green dots on session days (tool page, 1280 and 375) - derived from the product's mechanism, but rendered as a stock grid of bordered cells and confined to one screen.

unfinished: Placeholder thumbnails on show: every tool card on the find page has the same wrench glyph in a pale green square instead of a picture of the tool (items-ladder-3m default, all widths).
Identity is only the name in bold body text beside a tiny wrench glyph in the masthead; no focal point or typographic moment on any screen.
Browser-default controls in the filter panel: native yyyy/mm/dd date input with calendar icon and a native select of a different height (filters-open, 1280-light).
Half-empty right half at 1280/1440 on tool, confirm and done pages: content and form fields stop at ~700px with the right half blank; 'What happens next' box stops short at half width on done.
Footer band stops short with an empty grey band below on basket and done at 1280 (page shorter than viewport).
Truncated titles on phone find cards ('Cordless drill 18 V, co...') make the two drills indistinguishable (375-light).
Sections that are only a heading and text: 'Opening times' on find, 'Details' on tool.
Sticky reserve bar slices through the calendar in the tool page captures, hiding the second calendar row at 1280 and the pick-up hint at 375.
evidence: Find page 1280-light: first viewport is heading 'Find a tool', a paragraph, a search field and a 2-column grid of identical cards; nothing rewards a look.
Tool page 1280-light: title, a two-part definition list, a select and a bordered-cell calendar; no image of the drill.
Done page 1280-light: 'Reservation confirmed' as a plain heading over a definition-list card; no moment marking the reservation is made.
Clean and orderly throughout: consistent green, 4px radius, Avenir Next bold headings - it is tidy but bare, matching the 'community booking page with nothing of its own' counter-example.

x_evidence: deposit and availability on every card (find)
plain sentence-case labels, "Nothing is paid online" (confirm)
y_evidence: nothing pulls to corporate; but no element shows the practical world either (no tool photos)

x_evidence: copy only: "run by volunteers", "call the desk", "A volunteer will check the tool with you" (footer, done)
attributes.note: Neighbourly lives only in the copy; visually the pages read as an institutional public-service form (bordered boxes, error summary, grey-green neutrals), with no warmth from type, colour, imagery or the library's own artefacts (membership card, the room, the Saturday list).

y_evidence: carelessness visible: identical placeholder thumbnails, truncated phone titles making both drills read "Cordless drill 18 V, co...", misaligned double definition list on tool page, native filter controls, "Basket (1)" after confirming, reverse-ordered sessions with one stranded full-width card

brand_fit.weakest: neighbourly, not folksy - expressed in copy only; visuals say generic public-service form.
brand_fit.tone_check: Copy matches declared tone: matter-of-fact, casual-leaning, respectful, no exclamation marks.

mode_fit: All surfaces are Operate (done is Read). Low expression and conventional structure are correct here, and there is no hero moment or choreography. The issue is not too little expression for the mode but a missing identity floor: the name, the membership-card green and the library's own material appear nowhere as designed elements.

specificity.label: (judged)
specificity.anchor: 1: product content on a frame that fails the swap test
specificity.evidence: All three tests fail (see tests). Real copy (deposits, sessions, volunteer voice) sits on a frame that would carry any equipment-loan or booking service; the calendar Open tags are the only mechanism-derived element, rendered as a stock grid.

hierarchy.label: (judged)
hierarchy.anchor: 3: clear at main widths with one named lapse
hierarchy.evidence: Each page has one H1 and one filled button; primary/secondary/tertiary nameable on find, basket, confirm, done. Lapses: on find at 375 the search block drops below all ten cards; on find at 1280 the ten identical green thumbnails compete with the names; on tool the fixed action bar cuts across the calendar.

coherence.label: (judged)
coherence.evidence: One sans, one green, 4 px radius, borders throughout; dark theme keeps roles. Lapses: available badges lose their tinted background in dark (find 1280-dark) while later-date badges keep a grey one; filter panel uses native controls unlike the themed loan-length select; design.md says pills for badges but badges are 4 px.

restraint.label: (judged)
restraint.anchor: 2 cap: no focal point and no signature
restraint.evidence: No decoration without a job and no competing loud moves, but no signature or focal point on find, basket, confirm or done - restraint has become emptiness; capped at 2 per anchor.

brand_fit.label: (judged)
brand_fit.evidence: practical reflected; neighbourly only in copy; careful undermined by visible rough edges (see brand_fit).

execution.label: (judged)
execution.anchor: 2: clean at main widths, rough at edges
execution.evidence: Clean at 1280 light. Rough: phone titles truncated to indistinguishable stubs (find 375), two definition lists with different label columns (tool), stranded full-width session card and three-line wraps in narrow session cards (basket 1280), native date/select in filters, half-empty right side on tool/confirm/done, footer stopping short with empty band (basket, done 1280), dark badges lose tint.

appeal.label: (judged)
appeal.evidence: Matches verdict plain: identity only the name in bold body text; placeholder thumbnails; no typographic, imagery or colour moment on any screen; tidy throughout.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: No detector output would change the specificity or appeal verdicts. No SLP tells were flagged, consistent with my reading: the problem is an absence of decisions, not tells.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench glyph as a placeholder thumbnail
findings.description: On the find page each of the ten cards has an identical pale-green square containing the same wrench icon. The thumbnail slot that DESIGN.md calls "a thumbnail" carries no information about which tool it is.
findings.impact: The largest visual element on each card distinguishes nothing, so members comparing a drill with a sander may have to read every title; it is also the clearest sign of unfinish on the main screen and the place where the real tools could give the library its own look.

evidence.detail: all ten cards, thumbnail squares at x≈113 and x≈665

findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail must tell a member (which tool, which variant) and fill it with content that does that, or remove the slot.

findings.title: No identity or focal point on any surface
findings.description: The only identity is "Fernhill Tool Library" in bold body text beside a 16 px glyph. No surface has a typographic moment, imagery or a device drawn from the library's world; the membership-card green declared in DESIGN.md reads as a generic action green.
findings.impact: Members arriving from a link cannot tell visually that this is their neighbourhood library rather than any booking service; "neighbourly" is carried by copy alone.
findings.recommendation: Decide which element of the library's own world (the membership card, the desk, the session list) becomes the identity floor carried on every page, within Operate restraint.

findings.title: Tool titles truncate on phones so the two drills read identically
findings.description: At 375 every card title is cut with an ellipsis; "Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries" and "...one battery" both show "Cordless drill 18 V, co...".
findings.impact: On phones, the main device, members may open the wrong variant; the distinguishing words ("two batteries") are exactly what returning members look for.

evidence.detail: Corroborated by detector clipped-text hits on card h2 (TYP-15/A11Y-05/FUN-06)

findings.recommendation: Decide that tool names wrap rather than clip on narrow widths.

findings.title: Search block drops below all ten cards on phones
findings.description: At 375 the "Search tools" field, Search button and filter toggle appear after the full list, near the footer, whereas on desktop they sit above the list.
findings.impact: Members with a tool in mind on a phone must scroll past the whole catalogue to search; as stock grows this cost grows.

evidence.detail: Consistent with detector A11Y-03 focus-order jump from last card to Search tools

findings.recommendation: Decide the order of search and list by the find surface's job, the same at every width.

findings.title: Filter panel uses unthemed browser-default date and select controls
findings.description: With filters open, "Available from" is a native yyyy/mm/dd date field with the system calendar icon, and "Category" a native select with a different height and vertical offset from the date field.
findings.impact: The yyyy/mm/dd mask contradicts the declared date format ("Saturday 17 October") and the controls look unlike the themed loan-length list, a visible sign of unfinish.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the filter controls express the same system and date format as the rest of the flow.

findings.title: Fixed reserve bar cuts across the calendar on the tool page
findings.description: The white action bar with "Reserve this tool" overlays the second row of the pick-up calendar (dates 11-17, including Sat 17 "Open") in every tool capture at 1280 and covers the pick-up hint at 375.
findings.impact: The session days a member is choosing between may be hidden behind the bar, and the selected-day state is concealed (day-chosen, added).

evidence.detail: Detector A11Y-09 focused day buttons hidden behind div.actionbar; CMP-06 targets closer than 8 px

findings.recommendation: Decide how the bar and the calendar share the viewport so no session day is covered. Full-page capture may exaggerate the overlap; real-viewport behaviour not assessable from stills.

findings.title: Tool details split into two misaligned definition lists
findings.description: Under "Details" the first three rows (Category, Deposit, Available from) use a value column at x≈224, the next four (Chuck, Batteries, Weight, Case) at x≈180, with an extra gap between them.
findings.impact: Reads as two lists pasted together, weakening "careful"; members scanning specs lose the alignment that makes comparison quick.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether specs and loan facts are one table or two labelled groups, and align accordingly.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions in reverse date order with one stranded full-width card
findings.description: On basket at 1280 the sessions run Wed 28 Oct (alone, full width) then Sat 24 to Sat 10 in a row of five narrow cards whose text wraps to three lines.
findings.impact: The latest session gets the most prominence and the chosen pick-up date (Sat 17) sits mid-row; the reverse order and odd grid may lead members to pick the wrong session.
findings.recommendation: Decide session order and grid by how members think about dates and keep cards equal.

findings.title: Wide layouts leave the right half empty and footers stop short
findings.description: At 1280 tool, confirm and done keep content in a ~610 px column with the right half blank; "What happens next" on done stops at half width beside nothing; on basket and done the footer ends above the viewport bottom, leaving an empty grey band.
findings.impact: Desktop users in a lunch break see sparse, unfinished-looking pages; the summary card spans full width while the box below it does not, so the composition looks unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Decide one column logic for wide screens (a consistent measure for all blocks, or use the space for the reservation summary) and anchor the footer.

findings.title: Done page still shows "Basket (1)" after the reservation is confirmed
findings.impact: Members may wonder whether the tool is still waiting in the basket and whether the reservation really went through.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the basket shows once its contents become a reservation.

findings.title: Available badges lose their tint in dark mode
findings.description: In the dark theme the "Available from Sat 10 Oct" badges have no background and dim green text, while later-date badges keep a grey background, so the hierarchy between available-now and later is inverted.
findings.impact: Many members use dark mode on phones; the soonest-available tools, the ones they most want, get the least visible badges.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge so available-now stays the more prominent state.

findings.title: No-results search still shows the full catalogue on phones
findings.description: In the no-results state with "sewing machine" in the search field (375), all ten tools remain listed and no empty-state message is visible above them.
findings.impact: Members may think the search returned these tools or did nothing; the empty state, where the library could suggest asking the desk, is absent.
findings.recommendation: Decide what an empty search shows and where, at every width.

strengths: Copy is concrete and in the volunteer's voice ("Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence", "We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower").
Session calendar with Open tags / green dots ties the reservation to the desk's opening sessions - the product's real mechanism.
One filled action per page and a consistent type, radius and border system across five pages and two themes.
Error summary with linked, example-bearing messages ("like FT-01234").
keep: Keep the volunteer-desk copy voice and the session-day calendar concept; build identity from them rather than adding ornament.
notes: Isolated subagent. No baseline/ in packet, so pairwise not run (DES-05 not_applicable). Verdict file written before unseal; its written_at value (01:20Z) was an estimate rather than a clock reading - the unseal log (05:12:35Z) is authoritative and came after. Not all of the 320, 768, 1024, 1440, forced-colours and CVD captures were opened; judgements rest on 1280 light/dark and 375 light across all routes and states. Sticky-bar overlap is from full-page captures; real-viewport behaviour not assessable.
